text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fresh talks to resolve mutual flight ban by Nigeria and Britain fails as Nigeria rejects proposal to allow Nigerian planes, except those of national carrier, fly to Britain.
- A wooden pedestrian bridge collapsed in a suburb of Lagos on Monday killing no fewer than five people.
- Last week's termination of the contract of Ashland oil company has cut Nigerian oil output by 20,000 barrels per day, the volume the U.S. company was producing from its concessions.
- Normalcy returns to oil-producing town of Warri, where ethnic clashes flared again last weekend over relocation of local council headquarters killing 18 people.
- Nigerian military ruler General Sani Abacha and U.N. secretary-general Kofi Annan to jointly chair body to address technical requirements for Liberia's general election in July.
- Nigerian government deplores treatment of its nationals by United States and British embassies which it says collect fees from Nigerians and deny them visas.
- Fuel shortage worsens in Lagos and police say they will prosecute motorists who block highways in their search for petrol.
- Nigerian foreign reserves rise to $7 billion in May from $5.9 billion in March, say finance ministry sources.
